This runbook is the operational document for humans and AI monitoring agents:
how to run builds, what healthy output looks like, and how to interpret
failures and skips.

## Project facts (auto-generated)

- **Project:** `Singapore Law Watch`
- **Database file:** `sglawwatch.db` (Datasette database name: `sglawwatch`)
- **Title:** SG LawWatch
- **Description:** Non-commercial catalogue of Singapore legal news and reference content from the RSS feeds and public pages of Singapore Law Watch (https://www.singaporelawwatch.sg), a free daily legal news service of the Singapore Academy of Law (SAL): daily headlines with AI-generated summaries and links to the original articles, an index of law firm commentaries, and an index of the About Singapore Law reference chapters. This project is independent and is not affiliated with, or endorsed by, SAL, Singapore Law Watch, or any publisher. Copyright in the underlying articles belongs to the original publishers. Not openly licensed.

### Resources

| Resource | Description | Fragments | Fragments on skip | FTS fields |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `headlines` | Daily legal news headlines from the Singapore Law Watch Headlines RSS feed: title, link, publication metadata, full article text, and an AI-generated ~100-word summary per article. Append-only; entries more than 60 days old at ingest time, advertisement entries ('ADV:' titles), and already-seen IDs are skipped. The underlying articles are copyright their original publishers (e.g. The Straits Times, The Business Times, Lianhe Zaobao) — follow source_link for the original text. | no | no | `title`, `summary` |
| `about_singapore_law` | Catalog of 'About Singapore Law' reference chapters — academic overview chapters on Singapore law published on Singapore Law Watch, discovered from the Overview, Commercial Law, and Singapore Legal System section pages. One row per chapter; the chapter text itself lives in about_singapore_law_fragments. Chapters carry academic author bylines on the source pages and are copyright the Singapore Academy of Law and their credited authors. | yes | no | `title` |
| `about_singapore_law_fragments` | Searchable content chunks of each About Singapore Law chapter, scraped from the chapter page's .edn_article element. Each fragment is anchored on a numbered paragraph (e.g. '1.1.1'): preceding headings and lead paragraphs are joined forward onto it, while tables, lists, and indented paragraphs are appended backward onto the previous fragment. Footer and navigation content (contact lines, 'Tags:', chapter-navigation links, references) is filtered out. Chapter text is copyright the Singapore Academy of Law and the chapters' credited academic authors. | no | no | — |
| `commentaries` | Law firm commentaries on Singapore legal developments from the Singapore Law Watch Commentaries RSS feed. PDF links are converted to markdown via a self-hosted docling-serve instance; web links are extracted via Jina Reader. Append-only, keyed on the link URL. Copyright in each commentary belongs to its publishing law firm and authors — follow link for the original. | yes | no | `title`, `author`, `description`, `full_text` |
| `commentaries_fragments` | Fixed-size searchable chunks of each commentary's full_text: 1,200-character windows with 150 characters of overlap between consecutive chunks. When a commentary's full_text is empty (extraction failed), its RSS description becomes the sole fragment. Copyright in the underlying text belongs to the publishing law firm and authors. | no | no | — |

## Command reference (auto-generated)

```bash
uv run zeeker build                        # build all resources
uv run zeeker build <resource> [...]       # selective build
uv run zeeker build --sync-from-s3         # incremental: download existing DB from S3 first
uv run zeeker build --setup-fts            # (re)create FTS indexes on configured fields (idempotent)
uv run zeeker build --json                 # machine-readable BuildReport JSON on stdout
uv run zeeker build --progress-file p.json # atomic JSON snapshot after each resource (for watchers)
uv run zeeker build --fail-on-blocked      # exit 1 if any resource skipped with kind "blocked"
uv run zeeker deploy                       # upload the built .db to S3
```

## Status contract (auto-generated — zeeker 0.9.0)

This section is baked in verbatim from the installed zeeker version. Monitors
should parse builds against this contract, not against ad-hoc log scraping.

### Exit codes (`zeeker build`)

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | All resources succeeded (skips are not failures). |
| `1` | One or more resources failed, FTS setup failed, post-hook exited non-zero, `--fail-on-empty` with a skipped resource, or `--fail-on-blocked` with a resource that skipped with kind `blocked`. |
| `2` | Fatal error: schema conflict, DB open failure, config error, local-diverged sync. No coherent build ran. |

### Non-TTY line grammar (plain text output, what agents see)

One status line per resource, streamed as each finishes:

```
[OK  ] <resource>  <N> records  (<T>s)
[FAIL] <resource>  <error message>  (<T>s)
[SKIP] <resource>  <reason> (<kind>)  (<T>s)
[SKIP] <resource>  no data returned  (<T>s)
WARN[<resource>]: <message>
WARN[build]: <message>
SUMMARY: <S> succeeded, <F> failed, <K> skipped in <T>s | <k1>=<v1> <k2>=<v2>
FTS_ERROR: <message>
POST_HOOK: <command> exit=<code>
FATAL: <message>
```

- `[SKIP] name  <reason> (kind)` — the resource raised `Skip(reason, kind=...)`;
  the reason says WHY. `[SKIP] name  no data returned` is a plain `return []`
  skip (implicit kind `up_to_date`, no reason).
- Enrichment counters (see below) are appended to `[OK]`/`[SKIP]` lines as
  `; key=value key=value` (never to `[FAIL]` lines), e.g.
  `[SKIP] judgments  no data returned; updated=50 enriched=25  (12.3s)`.
- `WARN[<resource>]:` lines follow that resource's status line; `WARN[build]:`
  lines are build-level warnings (e.g. S3 sync issues).
- The `SUMMARY:` footer aggregates `extra_counts` across all resources after
  a ` | ` separator (omitted when there are no counters).

### Skip kinds and what each means for a monitor

| Kind | Meaning | Bumps `_zeeker_updates.last_updated`? | Monitor action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `up_to_date` | Source was checked; nothing new. The healthy steady state. | Yes | None. |
| `blocked` | A precondition failed (proxy down, missing env var) — the source was NOT checked. | No (time-based incremental resources stay safe) | Actionable: investigate the precondition. Use `--fail-on-blocked` to turn this into exit 1. |
| `disabled` | Intentionally switched off (feature flag / config). | No | None — not an incident. |

### Enrichment counters (`__zeeker_report__`)

Multi-phase resources that UPDATE existing rows (0 records inserted) report
work via a module-level dict in the resource module:

```python
def fetch_data(existing_table):
    global __zeeker_report__
    __zeeker_report__ = {"updated": 50, "enriched": 25, "notes": "phase2 drained 25"}
    return []
```

- Read and cleared on EVERY exit path — success, skip, even a fetch_data crash
  (work done before the crash stays visible).
- Re-read after the fragments phase; counters set in `fetch_fragments_data`
  merge in, summing on key collision.
- Int values only (other value types are ignored, never fail the build).
- Rendered as `key=value` on status lines, aggregated totals in the `SUMMARY:`
  footer, and carried as `extra_counts` / `notes` in `--json`.
- A "0 succeeded" SUMMARY with non-zero counters means real enrichment work
  happened — do not read it as a dead build.

### JSON payload (`--json` and `--progress-file` share the same schema)

Top-level fields:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | string | `success` \| `partial_failure` \| `failed` \| `fatal` |
| `total_duration_s` | float | Whole-build wall time. |
| `resources` | array | One object per resource (fields below). |
| `build_warnings` | array of strings | Build-level warnings (`WARN[build]:` lines). |
| `fts_error` | string or null | FTS setup failure, if any. |
| `fatal_error` | string or null | Set when the build died before/without a per-resource report. |
| `post_hook` | object or null | `{command, exit_code, stdout, stderr}` when `--post-hook` ran. |

Per-resource object fields:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | Resource name. |
| `status` | string | `success` \| `failed` \| `skipped` |
| `records` | int | New main-table rows inserted. |
| `duration_s` | float | Per-resource wall time. |
| `error_message` | string or null | Set on failure. |
| `traceback` | string or null | Full Python traceback on failure (paths CWD-relativized). |
| `fragments_records` | int or null | Fragment rows inserted, when a fragments phase ran. |
| `skip_reason` | string or null | The `Skip(...)` reason; null for plain returned-`[]` skips. |
| `skip_kind` | string or null | `up_to_date` \| `blocked` \| `disabled` (only meaningful when skipped). |
| `warnings` | array of strings | Per-resource warnings (`WARN[<resource>]:` lines). |
| `extra_counts` | object | Int counters from `__zeeker_report__`. |
| `notes` | string or null | Free-text note from `__zeeker_report__`. |

## What happens during a run

Three resources build in sequence. All use drop-and-retry semantics: an entry
whose extraction or summarisation fails is **excluded from the batch** (its ID
is never stored) so it is retried automatically on the next build — nothing is
ever stored with placeholder text or placeholder summaries.

### `headlines` (resources/headlines.py)

1. **Backfill pass** — rows already in the table with `summary IS NULL / '' /
   'None'` get a summary regenerated (plain HTTP fetch of the article + LLM).
   Runs before discovery on every build; logs `headlines: backfill: ...`.
2. **Discovery** — parses the Headlines RSS feed. Skips advertisements
   (`ADV:` titles), entries older than 60 days, entries at or before the DB's
   `MAX(date)`, and duplicate IDs. Per-skip reasons are logged and counted.
3. **Per-entry pipeline** (concurrent, LLM calls capped at 3 in flight) —
   fetch article text via Jina Reader, then generate a ~100-word summary via
   the OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint. Either step failing flags the entry
   and it is **dropped from the batch** with a
   `headlines: DEGRADED — dropped N/M entries for retry next build (...)`
   stderr warning plus one `dropped:` line per entry.
4. **Outcome**:
   - Some entries survive → `[OK  ] headlines  N records`; if any were
     dropped, the status line carries `dropped_jina=<n> dropped_llm=<m>`
     counters (via `__zeeker_report__`) and `notes` in `--json`.
   - New entries found but ALL dropped → **`Skip` kind `blocked`**:
     `[SKIP] headlines  all N new entries failed (Jina/LLM); retrying next
     build (blocked)`, still with the `dropped_*` counters. The freshness
     marker does NOT advance.
   - Genuinely nothing new → `[SKIP] headlines  no data returned`
     (`up_to_date`).

### `commentaries` (resources/commentaries.py + commentaries_fragments.py)

1. Parses the Commentaries RSS feed; skips already-imported links (MD5 of URL).
2. PDF links → docling-serve (`DOCLING_SERVE_URL`, max 2 concurrent
   conversions); web links → Jina Reader. Extraction failure stores the row
   with empty `full_text` (the fragment phase falls back to the RSS
   description as the sole fragment).
3. If >50% of new entries have empty text, logs
   `commentaries: WARNING — text extraction failed for X/Y entries; check
   docling health and JINA_API_TOKEN` on stderr.
4. Fragments phase chunks `full_text` into 1,200-char windows (150 overlap).

### `about_singapore_law` (resources/about_singapore_law.py + _fragments.py)

1. **Discovery** — fetches 3 section pages (Overview, Commercial Law,
   Singapore Legal System) and collects chapter links not already in the DB.
2. If **every** section fetch fails (proxy/network down) →
   **`Skip` kind `blocked`**: `[SKIP] about_singapore_law  discovery failed
   (proxy?): <TypeName>: <msg> (blocked)`. A partial failure (some sections
   reachable) proceeds with whatever was discovered. A clean crawl with no
   new chapters → `no data returned` (`up_to_date`) — the normal case, since
   chapters are rarely added.
3. Fragments phase scrapes each new chapter page and splits it into fragments
   anchored on numbered paragraphs (e.g. `1.1.1`).

Note (zeeker >= 0.9.0): `fetch_data()` runs ONCE per build; its output is
threaded to `fetch_fragments_data()` as `main_data_context` with no module
reload. The old double-invocation guards (PID sentinels) have been removed.

## Environment variables

All loaded automatically from `.env` by zeeker (see `.env.example`).

| Variable | Used by | Required? | When unset / broken |
|---|---|---|---|
| `JINA_API_TOKEN` | headlines, commentaries (web links) | Yes for content | headlines: Jina fetch returns empty → every new entry drops → `blocked` skip. commentaries: web-link extraction fails → rows stored with empty `full_text`. |
| `LLM_BASE_URL` | headlines (summaries, backfill) | Yes for summaries | Defaults to `https://api.openai.com/v1`. If the endpoint is down, every summary fails → new entries drop → `blocked` skip when nothing survives. |
| `LLM_API_KEY` | headlines | Cloud endpoints only | Defaults to `"ollama"` — local Ollama works without a key. |
| `LLM_MODEL` | headlines | No | Defaults to `gpt-4.1-mini`. |
| `TAILSCALE_PROXY` | headlines (LLM), about_singapore_law (site access from DC IPs) | Deployment-dependent | SOCKS5 proxy (`socks5h://...`) for reaching tailnet Ollama hosts; skipped for localhost targets. If the exit node is down, expect `blocked` skips. |
| `DOCLING_SERVE_URL` | commentaries (PDF extraction) | Yes for PDFs | Defaults to `http://localhost:5001`. Down → PDFs stored with empty `full_text` + the >50% WARNING. |
| `DOCLING_SERVE_API_KEY` | commentaries | No | Only if docling-serve enforces auth. |
| `DOCLING_CONCURRENCY` | commentaries | No | Default `2` in-flight conversions. |
| `ZEEKER_TOKEN_LOG` | headlines | No | JSONL token-usage log path (default `/workspace/agent/token_usage.jsonl`); failures are swallowed. |
| `S3_BUCKET`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `S3_ENDPOINT_URL` | `zeeker deploy` / `--sync-from-s3` | Deploy only | Build works without them. |

## Cadence & expected yield

Daily builds (host-side trigger).

| Resource | Normal new rows/run | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `headlines` | 0–10/day (2–5 weekdays, 0 weekends/holidays) | Skips 40+ ads and 60+ old entries per run — those skip logs are healthy. |
| `commentaries` | 0–3/day | 120+ already-imported entries skipped per run. |
| `about_singapore_law` | 0 most days (~46 chapters total, stable) | `no data returned` is the steady state. |

**Durations:** all-up-to-date run 5–10s; new headlines 20–30s; new
commentaries (PDF extraction) 80–180s; proxy timing out 200s+.

**Anomalies worth flagging:** any `blocked` skip; `dropped_jina`/`dropped_llm`
counters on several consecutive builds; the commentaries >50% extraction
WARNING; build duration > 5 minutes.

## Failure modes & recovery

No checkpoint files, quarantines, or on-disk caches in this repo — recovery is
always "fix the dependency, re-run the build". Dropped entries retry
automatically because their IDs were never stored.

| Symptom | Cause | Recovery |
|---|---|---|
| `[SKIP] headlines  all N new entries failed (Jina/LLM) (blocked)` with `dropped_jina` > 0 | Jina Reader down / `JINA_API_TOKEN` missing or expired | Fix token / wait out the outage; next build re-processes the same entries. |
| Same, with `dropped_llm` > 0 | LLM endpoint down (Ollama host offline, Tailscale exit node down) | Restore `LLM_BASE_URL` reachability; entries retry next build. |
| `[SKIP] about_singapore_law  discovery failed (proxy?) (blocked)` | singaporelawwatch.sg unreachable — usually the Tailscale proxy/exit node | Bring the proxy back; the crawl is idempotent. |
| `commentaries: WARNING — text extraction failed for X/Y` | docling-serve down (port 5001) or Jina failing | Rows are stored with empty `full_text`; fix the service — currently affected rows do NOT auto-heal (fragments fall back to the RSS description). Re-ingest by deleting the affected rows. |
| `headlines: backfill failed for ...` | Same LLM outage as above | Backfill re-attempts every build until the summary is non-empty. |
| Retry behaviour | Jina/docling calls use tenacity: 3 attempts, exponential backoff | 422s from Jina on `store.lawnet.com` / `utm_source=` URLs are expected and pre-skipped. |

**Skip vs failure cheat-sheet:** `up_to_date` skips are healthy (duration
0.1–5s). `blocked` skips are actionable outages (often 20–200s of retry time).
A `[FAIL]` means an unhandled exception — read the traceback in `--json`.

## Backlog / progress queries

```sql
-- Headlines missing summaries (backfill queue — should trend to 0)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM headlines
WHERE summary IS NULL OR summary = '' OR summary = 'None';

-- Commentaries with no extracted text (docling/Jina failures; no auto-heal)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM commentaries WHERE full_text IS NULL OR full_text = '';

-- Chapters with no fragments (fragment scrape failed at ingest)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM about_singapore_law a
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM about_singapore_law_fragments f WHERE f.item_id = a.id
);

-- Did the last build advance? (freshness markers; blocked skips do NOT bump these)
SELECT * FROM _zeeker_updates;

-- Recent ingest volume
SELECT DATE(imported_on) AS day, COUNT(*) FROM headlines
GROUP BY day ORDER BY day DESC LIMIT 14;
```

Approximate row counts as of Jul 2026: headlines ~833, commentaries ~201,
about_singapore_law ~46.

## Escalation

- One `blocked` skip is usually a transient outage — no action beyond noting
  it. The same resource `blocked` on **2+ consecutive daily builds** means a
  stuck dependency (Jina token, LLM host, Tailscale exit node, docling) —
  notify the maintainer.
- `zeeker build --fail-on-blocked` turns blocked skips into exit 1 for
  wrapper scripts that want hard failures.
- Token spend is logged to `ZEEKER_TOKEN_LOG` (JSONL) for LLM usage review.
- No dashboards or paging are wired up; the build log (and `--json` output)
  is the source of truth.
